Red Beans with Rice (Riz Collé ak Pwa Wouj)

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Serves 6-8Prep 20 min (plus overnight bean soaking)Cook 1 hr 30 min

Red Beans with Rice, known in Haitian Creole as Riz Collé ak Pwa Wouj, is a foundational dish in Haitian cuisine, symbolizing sustenance and the bounty of the earth. It is a particularly fitting offering and meal for Fete de Papa Zaka (Azaka Mede), the Feast of the Farmer Loa, who represents agriculture, harvest, and the hard work of the land. This hearty, flavorful dish honors Azaka's connection to the earth and provides nourishment for celebrants.

Ingredients

  • 1 pound (450 g) dried small red beans, soaked overnight or quick-soaked
  • 2 tablespoons vegetable oil
  • 1 large yellow onion, chopped
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 green bell pepper, cored and chopped
  • 2 scallions (green onions), chopped
  • 2 sprigs fresh thyme
  • 2 whole cloves
  • 1/2 Scotch bonnet pepper, whole or finely minced (optional, for heat)
  • 1 tablespoon tomato paste
  • 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, or to taste
  • 3 cups (600 g) long-grain white rice, rinsed
  • 6 cups (1.4 liters) water or reserved bean cooking liquid

Method

  1. If not already soaked, quick-soak beans by placing them in a large pot, covering with water by 2 inches (5 cm), bringing to a boil, boiling for 2 minutes, then removing from heat and letting stand for 1 hour. Drain and rinse.
  2. Place the soaked beans in a large pot with 8 cups (1.9 liters) of fresh water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until beans are tender, about 45-60 minutes. Drain the beans, reserving 4 cups (950 ml) of the cooking liquid.
  3. In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, garlic, and green bell pepper. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
  4. Stir in the chopped scallions, fresh thyme sprigs, whole cloves, and the Scotch bonnet pepper (if using). Cook for another 2 minutes until fragrant.
  5. Add the tomato paste to the pot and cook, stirring constantly, for 1-2 minutes to deepen its flavor.
  6. Stir in the cooked red beans, salt, and black pepper. Mix well to combine.
  7. Add the rinsed rice to the pot, stirring gently to ensure it's evenly distributed among the beans and seasonings.
  8. Pour in the 6 cups (1.4 liters) of reserved bean liquid or fresh water. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil.
  9. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot tightly, and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until all the liquid has been absorbed and the rice is tender.
  10. Remove the pot from the heat and let it rest, covered, for 10 minutes. Fluff the rice gently with a fork before serving.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, you can add a piece of smoked turkey or salted pork (rinsed well) to the beans while they simmer, removing it before adding the rice.
  • Adjust the amount of Scotch bonnet pepper to your desired level of heat; for less spice, omit it or add it whole and remove before serving.
  • A traditional Haitian seasoning base called 'epis' (a blend of garlic, onion, peppers, and herbs) can be prepared in advance and used in place of the individual aromatics for a more authentic flavor profile.
